rules.title: S.2983 An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting
rules.requirement: Pending Senate bill that would prohibit algorithmic rent setting. Reported favorably by the Housing Committee on 3/12/2026 and sent to Senate Ways and Means. It is not law; the page does not give operative text.
rules.key_value: pending ban on algorithmic rent setting
rules.quoted_span: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting
rules.review_note: Bill text not shown; specific prohibitions unknown.

rules.title: H.5222 An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market
rules.requirement: Pending House bill on algorithmic rent fixing in rental housing. Reported favorably by the Housing Committee on 3/12/2026 and sent to House Ways and Means. It is not law; operative text is not shown.
rules.key_value: pending bill on algorithmic rent fixing
rules.quoted_span: An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market

rules.title: State prohibition on local rent control
rules.requirement: Massachusetts cities and towns may not enact, maintain or enforce rent control. A narrow exception allows only voluntary, municipally compensated regulation of units owned by owners of ten or more units with fair market rent of $400 or less.
rules.key_value: Statewide ban on local rent control
rules.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date (stems from 1994 ballot Question 9).
rules.conflict_note: State bar may preempt any local rent control ordinance in Boston and Cambridge.

rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21 – statewide rent increase cap (blocked from ballot)
rules.requirement: The proposed initiative would have repealed the state ban on rent control and capped annual rent increases at the lesser of CPI or 5%. The SJC ruled it cannot appear on the November 2026 ballot, so it is not law.
rules.key_value: lesser of CPI or 5% annual cap (not enacted)
rules.quoted_span: Under the proposed law, annual rent increases would have been limited to the lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or 5%
rules.review_note: Struck by SJC in June 2026 (WBUR, D059); proponents hinted at 2028 refiling.

rules.title: Anti-discrimination: public assistance and housing subsidy recipients
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate against a person because they receive public assistance or a housing subsidy such as a voucher, or because of a requirement of that program. Other protected-class discrimination and inquiries in renting are also barred.
rules.key_value: ban on discrimination against public assistance / housing subsidy recipients
rules.quoted_span: For any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied two-family dwelling exemption in subsection 7

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment under written lease
rules.requirement: For nonpayment under a written lease, a landlord may end the lease with 14 days' written notice to quit. The tenant can stop it by paying all rent due with interest and costs by the answer day.
rules.key_value: 14 days' notice to quit; right to cure
rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease

rules.title: Notice to determine estate at will
rules.requirement: A tenancy at will ends with 3 months' written notice (or the rent interval/30 days if longer). For nonpayment, 14 days' notice to quit; a tenant with no similar notice in prior 12 months can cure by paying within 10 days.
rules.key_value: 3 months' notice; 14 days for nonpayment; 10-day cure
rules.quoted_span: In case of neglect or refusal to pay the rent due from a tenant at will, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the tenancy;

rules.title: Reprisal protections
rules.requirement: A landlord may not threaten or take reprisals against a tenant for enforcing housing laws, reporting violations or joining a tenants' union. Liability is 1-3 months' rent or actual damages plus fees; a termination notice, rent increase or substantial change within six months is presumed a reprisal.
rules.quoted_span: shall create a rebuttable presumption that such notice or other action is a reprisal against the tenant for engaging in such activities
rules.penalty: Damages of 1-3 months' rent or actual damages if greater, plus costs and attorney's fees

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment: required state form
rules.requirement: A written notice to quit for nonpayment must be accompanied by a state form listing rental assistance, court rules and eviction restrictions, with a statement that it is not an eviction. Courts will not accept a nonpayment summary process filing without proof of delivery of the form.
rules.key_value: state form required with nonpayment notice to quit
rules.quoted_span: No court having jurisdiction over an action for summary process pursuant to chapter 239, including the Boston municipal court department, shall, in an eviction for nonpayment of rent for a residential dwelling unit, accept for filing a writ, summons or complaint without proof of delivery of the form required under this section

rules.title: Security deposit limit and handling
rules.requirement: A deposit may not exceed the first month's rent. It must be held in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts account with a receipt and statement of condition, pay 5% annual interest (or bank rate if lower), and be returned within 30 days less itemized lawful deductions. Violations risk forfeiture and treble damages.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent cap; return within 30 days; 5% interest
rules.quoted_span: a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3) and that the tenant is given the statement of condition as required by subsection (2)
rules.effective_date_note: Original date not stated; 2025 amendment effective 2025-08-01 added agents and a fee-in-lieu option.
rules.penalty: Forfeiture of right to retain deposit; treble damages plus 5% interest, costs and attorney's fees

unverifiable_exemptions: vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less

rules.title: Limit on upfront charges at lease start
rules.requirement: Before a tenancy begins, a landlord or agent may require only first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of no more than one month's rent, and the cost of a key and lock. Application and screening fees by landlords are not permitted.
rules.key_value: Only first, last, 1-month deposit, lock and key
rules.quoted_span: At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:
rules.effective_date_note: Date the amendment extending the limit to agents took effect; the limit on lessors predates it (secondary source says since the 1970s).

unverifiable_exemptions: vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less

rules.review_note: Application-fee prohibition reading from secondary source D054; brokers treated separately.

rules.title: Broker fee allocation: only the party who engaged the broker pays
rules.requirement: A licensed broker may contract with either the tenant or the landlord, not both. Any fee must be paid only by the party who originally engaged the broker.
rules.key_value: Broker fee paid only by the party who hired the broker
rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson
rules.effective_date_note: Amended text effective August 1, 2025 per 2025, 9, Sec. 136.

no_rule_findings.finding: No enacted Massachusetts state law on algorithmic rent setting; only bills pending (S.2983, H.5222).
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: Bills banning the practice in the rental market are also working their way through the Massachusetts state House and Senate

no_rule_findings.finding: No statewide rent cap exists; the ballot initiative to repeal G.L. c. 40P and impose a cap was struck by the SJC and the statutory ban on rent control remains.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The petition would have repealed the Commonwealth’s existing statutory ban on rent control, G.L. c. 40P, and replaced it with a statewide cap on annual rent increases for most residential rental units

dropped_candidates.reason: 254 C.M.R. 7 is a broker licensing regulation known only from a secondary source; not a landlord rule and not stated by an official document

parsed.notes: MA state-level consolidation. D056 (803 CMR 5, CORI housing) is link-only; it is not added as a rule because I could not confirm its operative content from a readable document.
